root_cause.text: The conntrack netlink handlers accepted attacker-controlled SCTP state and expectation NAT direction attributes without validating them against their valid enum/range, letting invalid values reach `ct->proto.sctp.state` and `ct->master->tuplehash[...]` and trigger out-of-bounds access in `nf_conntrack_proto_sctp` and `nf_conntrack_netlink.c`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE` from plain `NLA_U8` to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., SCTP_CONNTRACK_HEARTBEAT_SENT)` and `CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR` from plain `NLA_U32` to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., IP_CT_DIR_REPLY)`, matching the CVE text that `nlattr_to_sctp()` wrote the user-supplied state directly and that `exp->dir = 100` caused `ct->master->tuplehash[100]` to read out of bounds.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE` from plain `NLA_U8` to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., SCTP_CONNTRACK_HEARTBEAT_SENT)` and `CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR` from plain `NLA_U32` to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., IP_CT_DIR_REPLY)`, matching the CVE text that `nlattr_to_sctp()` wrote the user-supplied state directly and that `exp->dir = 100` caused `ct->master->tuplehash[100]` to read out of bounds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten validation of the NAT direction netlink attribute to reject invalid direction values.
intent_record.what: The netlink policy for CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR was changed from accepting a generic NLA_U32 attribute to using NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_BE32, IP_CT_DIR_REPLY), while the CTA_EXPECT_NAT_TUPLE policy remained unchanged.
intent_record.how: This constrains the NAT direction attribute to a big-endian 32-bit value with an առավել maximum of IP_CT_DIR_REPLY, adding validation that rejects out-of-range direction values at parse time instead of accepting any 32-bit integer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an upper-bound validation for SCTP conntrack state netlink attributes.
intent_record.what: The SCTP netlink attribute policy for `CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE` was changed from a plain `NLA_U8` type declaration to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, SCTP_CONNTRACK_HEARTBEAT_SENT)`, adding an explicit upper bound for the allowed state value.
intent_record.how: At runtime, netlink validation will now reject SCTP state attributes whose numeric value exceeds `SCTP_CONNTRACK_HEARTBEAT_SENT`, preventing out-of-range conntrack SCTP state values from being accepted.

grouping_result.intent: Tighten validation of the NAT direction netlink attribute to reject invalid direction values.
Add an upper-bound validation for SCTP conntrack state netlink attributes.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause includes attacker-controlled expectation NAT direction attributes being accepted without range validation, leading to out-of-bounds access. This change explicitly tightens validation of the NAT direction netlink attribute, directly addressing part of the vulnerability.

The change adds upper-bound validation for SCTP conntrack state netlink attributes, which directly matches part of the root cause: attacker-controlled SCTP state values were accepted without range checks and could lead to out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This policy accepted an unbounded SCTP state attribute as only an 8-bit value, but did not restrict it to the valid enum range. That allowed attacker-controlled invalid state values to propagate into ct->proto.sctp.state and later cause out-of-bounds access.

This policy accepted the NAT direction attribute as a plain 32-bit value without validating that it matched the limited set of valid direction enums. Invalid directions could later be used to index ct->master->tuplehash[...] out of bounds.

vuln_statements.explanation: This netlink policy line accepted the SCTP state attribute as an unconstrained NLA_U8 value, allowing attacker-controlled invalid state values to reach ct->proto.sctp.state and later trigger out-of-bounds access.

This netlink policy line accepted the NAT direction attribute as an unconstrained NLA_U32 value, allowing invalid directions to propagate into ct->master->tuplehash[...] indexing and cause out-of-bounds access.
